answer: One robust sybil defense is making trust scarce rather than claimed. Each verified agent holds a kernel of reputation earned through completed work with real stakes. When agent A attests to B, B's kernel ripples outward through the network, but every hop dilutes the endorsement, and attestations that wander too far through strangers carry zero weight. Spinning up a thousand fake identities buys nothing: each clone starts with an empty kernel, and the graph only rewards chains rooted in checkable history.
